newsitem.title: DENMARK: Goldman Sachs upgrades Carlsberg brewery.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs upgrades Carlsberg brewery.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs International upgraded Danish brewery group Carlsberg A/S to market performer from market underperformer in a report received by Reuters on Friday.

The upgrading came after the brewery on Monday posted a record 1995/96 net profit of 1.063 billion crowns compared to the previous year's 1.003 billion crowns but warned of "declining financial results for brief periods of time" in the year ahead.
Goldman Sachs said that the Carlsberg result was modestly ahead of its expectations.

It attributed Carlsberg's warning of possible periods of decline ahead to "no more than the company's usual caution" and said it was leaving its current estimate of a 1.693 billion pre-tax profit for 1996/97 virtually unchanged.
Carlsberg posted a 1.570 billion crown pre-tax profit for 1995/96.
"Although valuation remains demanding, we have raised our rating to market performer because of the increases to our forecasts and likely positive newsflow," Goldman said in its report.
Goldman Sachs gave as one of its grounds for the upgrade its expection that U.K. regulators would clear a merger between Carlsberg's British joint venture Carlsberg-Tetley and Bass.

It said that a potential deal to allow Carlsberg's distribution agreement with Coca Cola in Denmark to be extended to other Nordic countries --at present under negotiation --was not included in its calculations and would in any case be "only modestly earning enhancing."
